title: Metsähallitus starts planning the Arctic Circle Hiking Area
seoTitle: Arctic Circle Hiking Area plan starts near Rovaniemi
description: Metsähallitus started management and tourism plans for the Arctic Circle Hiking Area in November 2026, and a public survey is open until the end of the year.
dek: The area took 130 000 visits last year, and the boardwalks on its mire trail are in such poor shape that Metsähallitus may not keep the route open next summer.
heroAlt: A narrow wooden boardwalk running through tall yellowing grass and low scrub on an open riverside meadow, with willows and birches behind it and a flat grey sky above.
heroCaption: A boardwalk on the island of Koivusaari in Rovaniemi in September 2022. The Arctic Circle Hiking Area and its mire nature trail lie about 25 kilometres north of the city.

body.text: In November 2026 Metsähallitus began drawing up two plans for the Arctic Circle Hiking Area: a management and use plan and a tourism plan. The planning area covers 3752 hectares along road 4 about 25 kilometres north of Rovaniemi and includes the Vianaava mire conservation site. The management plan will steer how the area is developed and how its different uses fit together for the next 10 to 15 years, and the tourism plan is drawn up together with the tourism operators of the area.

Visitors can have a say at this early stage. An online survey is open to users of the area, local residents and anyone else interested until the end of 2026, and representatives of stakeholder groups will be invited to workshops later in the process. The hiking area has many different user groups, so it is important that the different wishes can be reconciled, says Ilkka Vaara, senior specialist in land use at Parks & Wildlife Finland.

The planning starts on ground that is already under pressure. The Arctic Circle Hiking Area is the second most popular hiking area in Finland and one of the most visited nature destinations run by Metsähallitus, with 130 000 visits last year. Visitors divide evenly between the two rapids of the area, Vikaköngäs and Vaattunkiköngäs, and at both of them a suspension bridge carries walkers over the Raudanjoki river.
What the two suspension bridges ask of you

On both bridges the recommended gap between walkers is 5 metres, and no more than 10 people may be on a bridge at the same time. The signs that say so are small and worn. The instructions are followed unevenly and compliance can only be checked occasionally, says Jarmo Asell of Parks & Wildlife Finland, who adds that new and slightly larger signs are being put up in the coming weeks. A suspension bridge collapsed in Lieto in south-west Finland on Sunday 22 November and six people fell into the Aura river.

The condition of the bridges is checked every year by Metsähallitus itself, and an outside consultant makes a more thorough survey every 5 to 8 years. On the Arctic Circle bridges that survey was last made in 2023, and repairs are done as the need appears. Walkers' own observations carry weight, Asell says, because the in-house resources for inspections are limited, and the latest round of feedback was about the state of the signs.
The mire trail may not stay open next summer

Parks & Wildlife Finland has not been able to raise what it spends on the structures of the area at the pace at which tourism has grown, Asell says. That shows as wear on the ground in places, and as boardwalks that are not replaced as fast as they should be. The boardwalks of the mire nature trail, a 5.5 kilometre loop across the Vianaava mire, are in places in really bad condition, and next summer Metsähallitus has to consider whether it can keep the route open at all. The Könkäänvaara path in the same area was closed in November 2025 and taken off the map.

items: Leave 5 metres between you and the walker ahead on the suspension bridges, and wait your turn if 10 people are already on the bridge.
Start from the Vikaköngäs or the Vaattunkiköngäs car park. Both are kept clear in winter, and Vaattunkiköngäs has room for about 40 cars.
The trails have no winter maintenance, but the popular ones are usually packed down firm enough to walk.
Check the area's current notices before you drive out. The gravel road to Vaattunkiköngäs can close for a while during the spring thaw.
Tell Metsähallitus if you find a broken boardwalk, bridge or sign, because between the surveys the inspections lean largely on hikers' observations.
Answer the survey before the end of 2026 if you want the plans to take your kind of trip into account.

body.text: The hiking area is reindeer herding country. Dogs have to be kept on a leash, and walkers are asked to stay far enough from reindeer not to startle them.
The rapids, the mire and the old forests here are all within a day trip from Rovaniemi, and the same is true of several other routes in Lapland.
